rationale.conceptual: The method is an established, non-trivial DFT protocol (surface slabs, adsorption free energies via computational hydrogen electrode, electronic structure analysis). It requires domain knowledge to correctly set up the calculations (coverage, k-points, dipole correction, implicit solvation) but does not involve a novel algorithm or deep theoretical derivation; it is a careful reproduction of known results.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has multiple sequential stages: slab model building, geometry optimization, adsorption energy calculations, and electronic property extraction. While the paper reports additional process steps (Pourbaix diagram, XPS shifts), only two scored outputs are required. The orchestration is non-trivial (file management, convergence checks, post-processing scripts) but remains a standard computational workflow of moderate length.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires reproducing DFT adsorption energies and electronic descriptors for chalcogen-modified Cu(111) surfaces. The method is a standard application of plane-wave DFT with PBE-D2, PAW, and the computational hydrogen electrode, which is well-documented but demands careful setup of slab models, relaxation, dipole corrections, and post-processing. The execution involves a multi-stage pipeline (geometry optimization, adsorption energy calculations, Bader charge analysis, band center extraction), but the core scoring relies on a limited set of numbers. Overall moderate difficulty on both axes.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The DFT calculations involve small slab models (3×3 surface cells, 4 layers, ~100 atoms) with a plane-wave code. Typical memory requirements are a few GB; the input structures and reference data are negligible in size (a few kB). No GPU is required; a single CPU node suffices.
